question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` accept scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what exact wildcard grammar is allowed on the Gateway browser-origin authorization boundary?
rationale: This changes which browser origins may reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket authorization, and current docs intentionally describe full-origin allowlisting plus global `*` as the only wildcard policy.

options.title: Approve constrained wildcard grammar
options.body: Define a small allowed pattern set, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document positive and negative cases before accepting the feature.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus existing global `*` for intentionally broad local testing.

options.title: Defer to broader pattern design
options.body: Wait for loopback origin-pattern work to settle and decide whether Chrome extension scheme wildcards belong in the same contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained wildcard grammar
recommendation.body: Define a small allowed pattern set, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document positive and negative cases before accepting the feature.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and repeatedly hardened the Gateway origin-check boundary, making him the strongest routing candidate for the security/product decision.
